info.name: PayTrack API
info.description:
PayTrack microservices test collection.

Architecture:
- paytrack-gateway: Spring Cloud Gateway (http://localhost:8085) — the ONLY public entry point. Routes /api/payments/**, /api/accounts/** (→ payment-service) and /api/fraud/** (→ fraud-service). Secured with Keycloak JWT.
- payment-service & fraud-service: run inside the Docker network, NO host port published anymore. Reachable exclusively through the gateway.
- keycloak: http://localhost:8088 — identity provider (admin/admin).
- paytrack-registry: Eureka (http://localhost:8761) | paytrack-config: Config Server (http://localhost:8888) | kafka-ui: http://localhost:8090 — infra UIs, not behind the gateway, no token needed.

Security (Keycloak / OAuth2):
Every /api/** request requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The gateway validates the JWT signature against Keycloak (jwk-set-uri), and payment-service/fraud-service re-validate the same token independently (defense in depth).

One-time Keycloak setup before the API answers anything other than 401:
1) open http://localhost:8088 (admin/admin) and create a realm named exactly `paytrack`
2) create a client (access type public) e.g. `paytrack-web`, redirect URI http://localhost:3000/*, and enable Direct Access Grants (password grant, for manual testing)
3) create a test user
Then run "Keycloak Auth > Get Access Token": it stores the token in {{accessToken}}, and collection-level bearer auth applies it to every request automatically.

Default fraud rules (seeded into the fraud_configs table on fraud-service startup):
- HIGH_AMOUNT: reject transfers above 10,000 MAD
- REJECTION_RATE: reject after 3 rejected payments within 60 minutes
- VELOCITY: reject after 10 payments within 60 minutes

Workflow hint: accounts start with balance 0 — to test transfers successfully, deposit first (POST /api/accounts/{id}/deposit) or UPDATE the balance in the paymentdb accounts table (e.g. `UPDATE accounts SET balance = 1000 WHERE account_number = '<ACC-...>';`), otherwise every transfer fails with 'Insufficient balance'.

Setup: `docker compose up --build`, create the realm + client + user in Keycloak, then import this collection and the 'PayTrack Local' environment.

item.name: Keycloak Auth
item.description: Security is mandatory: every /api/** call returns 401 without a valid Keycloak JWT. Setup once in Keycloak (http://localhost:8088, admin/admin): 1) create a realm named exactly `paytrack`; 2) create a public client (e.g. paytrack-web) with Direct Access Grants enabled; 3) create a test user. Then run 'Get Access Token (password grant)' — it stores the token in {{accessToken}} and the OTHER collection-level auth applies it automatically to every request. Request-level 'noauth' is used below only to prove 401 behavior and public non-API routes.

request.description: OIDC discovery document served by Keycloak for the `paytrack` realm. Only exists after the realm is created. Lists token endpoint, authorization endpoint and the JWKS URL the apps use to validate signatures.

Exchanges username/password for a JWT access token (S256 realm signing key). Stores access_token in the {{accessToken}} environment variable, which the collection-level Bearer auth uses on every API call. Returns 401/400 if the client lacks Direct Access Grants or the user doesn't exist.
Sends NO Authorization header (auth overridden to noauth). Expected 401: Spring Security requires the JWT. Proof that the API is closed without a token.

Swagger UI is whitelisted in the gateway security config (no token needed). From here you can call 'Authorize' and paste the access token to try the endpoints. Expected 200 (redirect to /swagger-ui/...).

exec: pm.test("Swagger UI is reachable without auth", function () {

item.name: Payment Service
item.description: REST API exposed by payment-service under /api/payments/** and /api/accounts/**. Everything is accessed through the API Gateway (port 8085); payment-service no longer publishes a host port, so there is no direct path from outside. All calls require the Bearer token (set by 'Keycloak Auth').

request.description: Initiates a transfer. Returns a PENDING TransferResponse (UUID transferId) and stores the transferId in a collection variable for use by GET /api/payments/{id}. The payment then goes through fraud-service via Kafka (fraud.fraud-check → payment.initiated).
Expected 400 (BAD_REQUEST): 'The source and destination accounts must be different.'

exec: pm.test("Message mentions accounts must be different", function () {

request.description: Expected 400: 'Source account not found: ACC-99999'. A `payment.failed` Kafka event is also sent.
Expected 400: 'Destination account not found: ACC-99999'.
Expected 400: 'Insufficient balance or source account is inactive.' Accounts are created with balance 0, so deposit first or raise the source account balance in the DB (see collection description).
Bean validation: `@NotBlank` on fromAccountNumber -> 'The source account is required'.

Bean validation: `@DecimalMax(10000.00)` on TransferRequest -> 'The amount cannot exceed 10,000 MAD'. Note: this guard lives in payment-service; fraud-service independently REJECTs high amounts over its own HIGH_AMOUNT config threshold (default 10,000 MAD).
Bean validation: `@DecimalMin(0.01)` -> 'The amount must be greater than 0'.

query.description: Optional. One of: PENDING, PROCESSED, FAILED, FRAUD, REJECTED, COMPLETED, DLT

request.description: Paginated payment list (Pageable default size=20, sort=createdAt,desc). All filter fields optional (PaymentFilter).
Fetch a single payment by UUID. The {{transferId}} variable is set automatically by 'Transfer - Happy Path (via Gateway)'. Expected: PaymentDto with status, amount, accountId, createdAt.
Aggregated stats: totalPayments, totalAmount, successful/pending/failed counts and amounts, averageAmount, paymentsByStatus map.

Server-Sent Events stream. Sends a `connected` event immediately, then a `payment` event each time a payment is processed. Timeout is 30 minutes. Note: in the Postman UI the connection stays open — use the console to view events, or open this URL in a browser (server sent events via GET).

item.name: Accounts
item.description:
Account management under /api/accounts/** — routed through the gateway (→ payment-service). Account numbers are auto-generated (ACC-########). New accounts start with balance = 0, status = ACTIVE. The {{accountId}} and {{accountNumber}} variables are set automatically by "Create Account".

Lifecycle: ACTIVE -> deactivate -> INACTIVE, ACTIVE/INACTIVE -> block -> BLOCKED, unblock -> ACTIVE. An account can only be closed (DELETE or POST /close) when its balance is zero. Deposit/withdraw mutate the balance directly. The statement lists payments where the account is the source (DEBIT) or destination (CREDIT).

request.description: Creates an account. Expected 201 CREATED with AccountDto (auto-generated accountNumber, balance=0, status=ACTIVE, currency=MAD). Stores id -> {{accountId}} and accountNumber -> {{accountNumber}}.
Expected 400: 'An account already exists with this email'. Run 'Create Account' first, or adapt the email.
Bean validation: `@Email` on ownerEmail and `@Size(min=3,max=3)` on currency.

query.description: Optional. One of: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, BLOCKED, CLOSED

request.description: Paginated list of accounts with optional filters: ?status=ACTIVE and/or ?ownerEmail=... (partial match, case-insensitive). Default page size=20, sort=createdAt,desc.
Fetch a single account by UUID ({{accountId}}), set by "Create Account". Returns AccountDto.
Fetch an account by its auto-generated number ({{accountNumber}}).
Fetch an account by the unique owner email. Expected 400 if it does not exist.
Full update. Only non-null fields are applied. Expected 200 with updated AccountDto.
Partial update — only the provided fields are applied.
Soft-closes the account (status -> CLOSED). Requires balance = 0, otherwise 400/409. Returns 204 No Content.
ACTIVE transition. Only valid from INACTIVE (use /unblock from BLOCKED). Returns AccountDto.
INACTIVE transition. Only valid from ACTIVE. Returns AccountDto.
BLOCKED transition. Only valid from ACTIVE/INACTIVE (used by fraud flows). Returns AccountDto.
ACTIVE transition from BLOCKED. Returns AccountDto.
CLOSED transition (same rule as DELETE: balance must be 0). Returns AccountDto.
Credits the account balance (amount > 0). Accounts start at 0 — use this to fund wallets for transfer tests. Returns AccountDto with the new balance.
Debits the account balance. Only ACTIVE accounts; amount must be <= balance. Returns AccountDto with the new balance.
Live balance snapshot: accountNumber, ownerName, balance, currency, status, updatedAt.
Paginated statement of payments involving the account (source = DEBIT, destination = CREDIT). Query: page, size, sort.

item.name: Fraud Service
item.description:
fraud-service REST API under /api/fraud/** — accessed through the gateway only. The detection engine consumes `fraud.fraud-check` (published by payment-service on transfer), evaluates the transaction against the current fraud_configs rules (FraudDecision APPROVED/REJECTED), persists a fraud_evaluations row and publishes the result onward for payment-service to finalize.

Configuration management (fraud_configs table): one row per rule type (HIGH_AMOUNT / REJECTION_RATE / VELOCITY). Defaults are seeded on startup; the detection reads them live. A config can be listed, created (one per rule type — otherwise conflict), updated, toggled on/off, deleted (rule then falls back to its built-in default) or reset to defaults. Use kafka-ui (http://localhost:8090) to inspect topics: payment.initiated, payment.processed, payment.failed, payment.DLT, payment.fraud, fraud.fraud-check, fraud.fraud-evaluated.

item.name: Fraud Configs
item.description: CRUD for the fraud detection rules used by the evaluator.

request.description: Lists all fraud configs (sorted by ruleType). Each item: id (UUID), ruleType (HIGH_AMOUNT|REJECTION_RATE|VELOCITY), enabled, threshold, windowMinutes, description, updatedBy, createdAt, updatedAt. Stores the first config id in {{fraudConfigId}} for the other requests.

exec: pm.test("Returns an array of configs", function () {

request.description: Fetch a single fraud config by UUID ({{fraudConfigId}}, set by 'Configs - List').

Creates a fraud config. Expected 201 CREATED. Only one config per ruleType: since the three defaults are seeded on startup, expect 400 'A fraud config already exists for rule type: HIGH_AMOUNT' — delete an existing rule first (or use PUT /{id} to modify it instead). Count-based rules (REJECTION_RATE, VELOCITY) require a whole-number threshold and windowMinutes. Sets {{fraudConfigId}} on success.

Modifies a fraud config — only non-null fields are applied. Expected 200 with the updated FraudConfigDto. Tweak the threshold (e.g. 20,000 MAD) and observe the HIGH_AMOUNT rule change on the next transfer above the new value.
Flips the `enabled` flag. A disabled rule is ignored by the evaluator. Expected 200 with the updated FraudConfigDto.
Deletes a fraud config. Expected 204 No Content. The related rule then falls back to its built-in default during evaluation; the seeder re-creates missing defaults on the next fraud-service restart.

Resets every rule to its default threshold/window and re-creates any missing rules: HIGH_AMOUNT=10000 MAD, REJECTION_RATE=3 rejects / 60 min, VELOCITY=10 payments / 60 min. All rules are re-enabled. Returns the full config list.

query.description: Optional. Number of rows, clamped to 0..500 (default 100)

request.description: Latest fraud evaluations, newest first. Each item: id, paymentId, accountId, amount, currency, decision (APPROVED|REJECTED), reason, evaluatedAt.
Same as list but only REJECTED evaluations (the fraud alerts shown in the UI).
Aggregated counters: totalEvaluations, approvedCount, rejectedCount.

item.description: Supporting services used to verify the platform is up.

request.description: Eureka dashboard HTML. Shows registered instances of payment-service, fraud-service, paytrack-gateway.
Returns JSON of all registered services. `applications.application` should include PAYMENT-SERVICE, FRAUD-SERVICE, PAYTRACK-GATEWAY.
Instance details for payment-service (host, port, status).
Configuration served for payment-service (datasource, kafka, eureka).
Configuration served for fraud-service.
Kafka UI dashboard (provectuslabs/kafka-ui). Inspect topics, consumers (payment-group, fraud-group), and messages.
